captions: The nets are full. The crates pile up.
Down in the village, the adhan rises.
Nobody looks up. “The olives won’t wait.”
Every Friday this autumn: one more crate.
Then your little cousin tugs your sleeve: “Aren’t we going?”
You put the crate down. Oil still on your hands.
The fountain. Cold water. The dust runs off your wrists.
Row two. The khutbah begins. The olives can wait.

post.caption:
Friday, 12:50. 3 crates left. Jumu’ah starts at 1. 🤍

Your uncle’s olive grove, the best harvest in years. The adhan rises from the village, and nobody looks up: “Allah will understand. The olives won’t wait.” Every Friday this autumn, one more crate. Until your little cousin tugs your sleeve: “Aren’t we going?”

“O you who have believed, when [the adhan] is called for the prayer on the day of Jumu'ah [Friday], then proceed to the remembrance of Allah and leave trade.” (62:9)

Today at 1: leave the crate, the laptop, the till. Go to Jumu’ah.
